links.outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT pDDI outputs across repeated runs on 50 patients
links.effect: Reproducibility was limited, with ChatGPT-5 achieving only 68% consistency across repeated runs.
links.quote: Reproducibility was also limited, with ChatGPT-5 achieving only 68% consistency across repeated runs.

links.outcome: ChatGPT pDDI detection versus standard interaction checkers, discrimination and clinical utility
links.effect: ChatGPT identified fewer interactions than standard databases (8 and 10 vs. 22 total; 1 and 2 vs. 4 significant per patient); none outperformed standard tools in discrimination or clinical utility.
links.quote: None of the versions outperformed standard tools in discrimination or clinical utility.

screen.reason: Retrospective cohort evaluation of LLMs (ChatGPT-4.1 and ChatGPT-5) for detecting drug-drug interactions in ICU patients compared against reference databases and clinical outcomes, without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
